text_blocks.snippet: Pancytopenia, a condition where there is a deficiency in all three blood cell types (red blood cells, white blood cells, and platelets), can be caused by certain medications. Some medications known to cause pancytopenia include chemotherapeutic agents, certain antibiotics (like chloramphenicol, sulfonamides, linezolid), antiepileptic drugs (like carbamazepine, valproate), and immunosuppressants (like azathioprine, methotrexate).
